lead: Money and money-like collectables (coins, bullion, banknotes, stamps and postal items, trading cards, tokens and medals, orders and decorations, trophies) plus the holders and albums that keep them; organised by object type, then issuer and catalogue number (KM, RIC, Pick, SG, Scott, Michel), with grades from the grading-services register, issuers in the issuer register and period/ancient coinage as a view.

b.v: catalogue number (KM, RIC, Crawford, Pick, SG, Scott, Michel, set and card number)
b.w: Every collecting field prices by its standard catalogue; identification comes before grade.

b.v: third-party slab (PCGS, NGC, PMG, PSA, BGS, CGC, SGC) > raw
b.w: Grading-services register; the grader's name and scale travel with the grade.
Counterfeits, reprints and fantasy pieces are common in every field; certificates and pedigrees add value.

depts.note: Issuer → type (catalogue number) → date/mint mark → die variety → grade; ancient and traditional coinage is also a period view.

b.v: Mint State 70 down to About Uncirculated, Extremely Fine, Very Fine, Fine, Very Good, Good, About Good, Fair, Poor (Sheldon scale)
b.w: Looked at first; proof and uncirculated describe how the coin was made, not its condition.

b.m: Strike, contact marks, lustre, eye appeal
b.w: Weighed after wear, in that order.
Add rarity; die varieties are the variant forms of a coin.

s.brief: Turn the flat issuer lists into archetypes = coin types (Morgan dollar, Peace dollar, Walking Liberty half, Mercury dime, Buffalo nickel, Lincoln cent, Sovereign, Maria Theresa thaler, Spanish dollar, Napoléon d'or, Vreneli, Krugerrand-era ZAR pond, 500 yen, Loonie, Yuan Shikai dollar), each with mk = issuing mint/authority (issuer register), catalogue number (KM where sourced) and key versions (key dates, mint marks, notable die varieties). Order by significance, not alphabet. Commemorative programmes (50 State Quarters, 2 euro commemoratives, America the Beautiful, Canada 150, Japan 47 prefectures) become archetypes of the circulating commemorative kind. Collector coins: add NCLT archetypes (US commemorative half dollars, Royal Mint proof sovereigns, RCM lunar silver). Proof/mint sets: US proof set, Royal Mint annual sets, Japan mint sets. Add Mint error coin (off-centre, double die, broadstrike; e.g. 1955 doubled-die cent) as a new kind. Die variety, finish (proof, reverse proof, BU, matte) and mint mark are types, not kinds.

k.brief: Archetype per coin type; junk silver is a type.
Non-circulating legal tender; proof/reverse-proof/high-relief as types.
Replace the bullion-dealer source with mint or reference pages.
New: error types (off-centre, double die, clipped planchet, mule, wrong planchet) as types; famous errors as archetypes.
Siege pieces (Newark, Pontefract, Scarborough, Leiden) and Kriegsgeld/Notgeld coins as archetypes.

s.brief: New shelf (findings: ancient/traditional coinage view). Archetypes from Wikipedia/Wikidata/reference catalogues (RIC, Crawford, Sear, Hartill, Album): Athenian owl tetradrachm, Aegina turtle, Alexander tetradrachm; Roman Republican denarius (Crawford), Roman Imperial aureus/denarius/sestertius/antoninianus/follis (RIC), Eid Mar denarius; Byzantine solidus/histamenon; Celtic staters; English hammered penny (long cross, short cross), groat, noble; Islamic dinar/dirham (Umayyad reform); Chinese cash coin (Kaiyuan Tongbao), knife and spade money; Japanese koban/oban and mon; Indian punch-marked coins, Mughal mohur/rupee. Odd & curious money (Kissi penny, manilla, Yap rai stone, ring money) as one kind. Keep each kind to 3–8 archetypes; catalogue reference in dt.

k.brief: Include knife and spade money as archetypes.
Pre-coinage and commodity money: manilla, Kissi penny, cowrie, Yap stone, bronze ring money.

depts.note: Major sovereign programmes and refiners only; small-nation wildlife issues are leftovers, not archetypes.

b.w: Stated with its standard.
Second.

b.v: sovereign mint or LBMA good-delivery refiner > unlisted refiner
b.w: Liquidity on resale depends on a recognised maker.
A price, so not listed with the product.

s.brief: Bullion major programmes as archetypes (findings): Krugerrand (originator, 1967), Canadian Maple Leaf, American Gold Eagle, American Silver Eagle, American Buffalo, Britannia, Australian Kangaroo/Nugget, Kookaburra, Koala, Perth Lunar series, Chinese Panda, Vienna Philharmonic, Mexican Libertad, Queen's Beasts, Somali Elephant; versions = metals and notable redesigns (e.g. Silver Eagle type 2, Britannia security features). Cut the ~70-item list to these; minor wildlife issues drop or stay as m. Bars: archetypes PAMP Lady Fortuna, Valcambi CombiBar, Argor-Heraeus Kinebar, Perth/Royal Mint minted bars; cast vs minted as types. Rounds: generic designs (Walking Liberty, Buffalo, Morgan) and makers (Sunshine Minting, Scottsdale, Intaglio). Brand register: PAMP, Valcambi, Argor-Heraeus, Heraeus, Perth Mint, Royal Mint, RCM, US Mint, South African Mint (use issuer names).

depts.note: Issuer → series → denomination (Pick number) → signature/prefix variety → grade.

b.w: Taken from the stored notes; graders in the grading-services register.

s.brief: Turn the series lists into archetypes per issuer series (Bank of England Series A–G, Bank of Japan series, renminbi series 1–5, Swiss National Bank series, Banxico families, Bank of Canada series, euro first and Europa series, US Federal Reserve Note / large-size notes, Australian polymer series) with Pick numbers where sourced and versions = denominations/signature varieties. Rename 'Obsolete banknote' to cover private and local bank notes (Scottish and Northern Irish bank notes are current, not obsolete; US obsolete and National Bank Notes). Merge facsimile/counterfeit and prop/souvenir notes into one kind. Add new: Military and occupation currency (US MPCs, Allied Military Currency, Japanese invasion money), Error note (missing print, cutting errors). Star/replacement notes and fancy serials are types. Notgeld and Zimbabwe bearer cheques stay under emergency scrip as archetypes.

k.brief: New kind; move the Japanese occupation and Hawaii overprint items from emergency scrip here.

Thins, tears, repairs, re-perforation, regumming.

s.brief: Archetypes = named issues/designs, ordered by significance: Penny Black (originator, 1840), Penny Red, Basel Dove, Bull's Eye, Cape Triangular, Mauritius Post Office, Hawaiian Missionaries, Machin, Wilding, Germania, Semeuse, Marianne, Washington–Franklin, Prexies, Large Queens; versions = plates, perforations, watermarks with SG/Scott/Michel numbers where sourced. Commemoratives: Columbian Issue, Zeppelin issues, Silver Jubilee. Add new kinds: Stamp error and variety (Inverted Jenny, Treskilling Yellow colour error, British Guiana 1c magenta as a unique rarity if sourced; inverts, missing colours, imperforates as types); Airmail stamp; Cinderella and poster stamp (Christmas seals, Reklamemarken, local posts). Revenue stamps keep Duck Stamp and US revenue archetypes. Perforation, watermark, shade, plate number, coil/sheet/block format are types, not kinds.

Postal history (findings): add Postal history cover (stampless and early covers, rates and routes, censored and disaster mail), Flight and rocket cover (first-flight, Zeppelin, crash covers), Postmark and cancellation (Maltese Cross, slogan, machine cancels) and Maximum card. First-day covers: cachet makers (e.g. Artcraft, Fleetwood) as archetypes if sourced. Postal stationery: Mulready envelope, Nesbitt/Plimpton series, Korrespondenz-Karte (first postal card, 1869), aerograms. Keep definitions plain.

Archetypes = sets/lines and icon cards, by significance: T206 (Honus Wagner), Goudey 1933, 1952 Topps (Mantle #311), 1986 Fleer Jordan #57, 1989 Upper Deck Griffey, Topps Chrome, Bowman Chrome (1st Bowman), Panini Prizm, National Treasures, Exquisite; makers Topps, Panini, Upper Deck, Fleer, Donruss, Bowman in the brand register. Cut the Topps Chrome insert-name list (26 SKU-level names) to a few representative versions. Split old insert/autograph kind into Insert, Autograph and Relic kinds; add Rookie card, Parallel (refractor, Prizm colours, printing plates, 1/1 as types) and Vintage tobacco and candy card.

LOB (Blue-Eyes White Dragon), One Piece Card Game; non-sports: Garbage Pail Kids, Star Wars (Topps 1977), Marvel Universe; cigarette and trade cards (Wills, Player's, Ogden's, Liebig, Brooke Bond tea cards). s.brief: Add archetypes: Conder tokens (18th-century British trade tokens), US Hard Times and Civil War tokens, Bavarian/German Notgeld tokens, NYC subway token, telephone tokens (Italian gettone), Communion tokens (Scotland), shopping-cart tokens. Add new kinds: Casino chip and gaming token (casino chip collecting), Love token and counterstamped coin, Encased coin (encased postage, encased cents). Coin weight moves here from holders (antique coin weights are collected as exonumia).

Archetypes: US so-called dollars, British historical medals (coronation and jubilee medals), Paris Mint (Monnaie de Paris) art medals, Art Nouveau plaquettes (Roty, Chaplain), Medallic Art Company, Franklin Mint medals; Olympic winners' and participation medals under award medal; elongated (pressed) pennies as a separate kind split from souvenir medal; challenge coins (military unit coins). Medallic-art makers into the brand register.

s.brief: Archetypes from the existing lists, ordered by precedence: Victoria Cross, George Cross, DSO, DSC, Albert Medal; Order of the Garter/Bath/St Michael and St George/British Empire/Royal Victorian Order; Waterloo Medal, Crimea, Indian Mutiny, Queen's South Africa, 1914 Star / British War Medal / Victory Medal trio (Pip, Squeak and Wilfred), WWII stars, GSM 1918–62 and 1962–2007; long-service medals. Clasps and classes as versions.

Archetypes: Medal of Honor (Army, Navy, Air Force versions), Distinguished Service Cross / Navy Cross, Silver Star, Bronze Star, Purple Heart, Legion of Merit; campaign and service medals (Civil War, WWI Victory Medal, WWII theatre medals, Vietnam Service, Good Conduct). Use the Institute of Heraldry / Wikipedia pages.

Medals by state: France (Légion d'honneur, Médaille militaire, Croix de guerre), Germany and Prussia (Iron Cross 1813/1870/1914/1939, Pour le Mérite, Order of the Red Eagle), Russia and USSR (Order of St George, Order of Lenin, Hero of the Soviet Union, Order of the Red Star, Order of the Patriotic War), Japan (Order of the Rising Sun, Order of the Golden Kite, Sacred Treasure), plus other notable national orders (Order of the Golden Fleece, Order of the Elephant). Keep 3–8 archetypes per kind.

s.brief: Exactly four kinds. Grading slab: archetypes per grader (PCGS, NGC, ANACS, PMG, PCGS Banknote, PSA, BGS, SGC, CGC Cards) with slab generations as versions where sourced (e.g. PCGS rattler, NGC fatty); graders go to the grading-services register. Coin and note holder: capsules (Air-Tite), 2x2 flips, cardboard 2x2s, Mylar currency sleeves as types. Card holder: merge toploader, penny sleeve and other card holders (one-touch magnetic, semi-rigid card saver as types; BCW, Ultra PRO, Cardboard Gold as makers). Stamp mount and hinge: merge (Hawid, Showgard, Prinz mounts; hinges as type).
